ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an AC power source symbol, connected to the upper and lower two wire rails. In the middle and on the right side, there is respectively a branch composed of a diode and a capacitor; the directions of the two diodes are opposite, and the two capacitors are respectively connected in the lower area; “Output” is marked between the middle nodes of the two branches. Reasoning: Since the directions of the two diodes are opposite, they will conduct respectively during opposite half-cycles of the AC input, causing the two capacitors to be charged respectively to a voltage approximately equal to the AC peak value, and the output is taken from the position where the voltages of the two capacitors are added. Therefore, the function of this circuit is to raise the output voltage to approximately twice the peak value, and it belongs to a voltage-doubling structure.

method.method_draft: First inspect the circuit diagram: identify the left element as an AC source feeding top and bottom rails. Then note the two diode-capacitor branches and the output taken between their intermediate nodes. Because the diodes conduct on opposite half-cycles, each capacitor charges to approximately the AC peak with opposite reference polarities, and the output is the sum of the two stored capacitor voltages. Therefore the circuit is best described as a voltage doubler.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as an AC source connected across top and bottom rails, with two vertical branches on the right. Each branch contains a diode and a capacitor, and the output terminals are taken from the midpoints between the diode/capacitor sections. The two diodes are oriented oppositely so the two capacitors charge on alternate half-cycles.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to determine that a short circuit classification is required, not a numerical calculation.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rule that a pair of oppositely oriented diode-capacitor rectifier sections driven by an AC source, with the output taken so the capacitor voltages add, is a voltage multiplier of factor two, commonly called a voltage doubler.
